selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a coherent cow/leather-themed progression. The player must first feed a cow (requiring wheat and locating a cow), then craft a leather chestplate (requiring leather obtained from cows in the area, plus a crafting table), and finally sell leather to a leatherworker villager. Feeding the cow first ensures the player locates and interacts with cows before harvesting leather for crafting and selling. The craft and sell tasks both depend on the cow interaction but are also sequentially linked since the player must manage limited leather resources between crafting (8 leather) and selling.

edges.reason: Feeding the cow establishes cow location and interaction; leather from cows is needed to craft the leather chestplate (8 leather required)
Feeding the cow establishes cow area familiarity; leather obtained from cows is needed to sell to the leatherworker villager
Crafting the chestplate first ensures the player uses leather for crafting before selling remaining leather to the villager, managing limited resources

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because feeding a cow requires the player to approach within interaction range (~3 blocks) and face the cow while holding wheat. No 'use_item' rule type is available in the evaluator, so this proximity+facing check is the best available proxy. The target is Cow 1 at spawn-relative (-3, 0, -3), verified in sandbox. The cow has NoAI:1b so it remains stationary at this position. max_distance=3 matches Minecraft's interaction range, and facing_tolerance=90 ensures the player is oriented toward the cow.

Uses inventory_has because the crafted leather chestplate ends up in the player's inventory. The player starts with 0 leather chestplates (verified in inventory screenshot — only wheat, leather, and emeralds present). Having at least 1 leather_chestplate definitively confirms the crafting task was completed. This is the gold-standard rule for craft tasks.

Uses inventory_has for emeralds because selling leather to the novice leatherworker villager exchanges 6 leather for 1 emerald. The player starts with exactly 5 emeralds (verified in inventory screenshot). After completing one trade, the player will have 6 emeralds. Since there are no other emerald sources in the scene (no ore, no other villagers, no loot chests), reaching min_count=6 emeralds definitively confirms the leather sale occurred.

scene_description: A flat grassy area with two stationary cows, a crafting table, a cauldron (leatherworker job site), and a leatherworker villager. The player starts with wheat (to feed cows), leather (for crafting and selling), and emeralds. The scene supports the sequential tasks: feed a cow with wheat, craft a leather chestplate at the crafting table, and sell leather to the leatherworker villager.
task_text: First, feed a cow using wheat. Then, craft a leather chestplate at the crafting table. Finally, sell leather to the leatherworker villager.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin. Cows are ~4 blocks to the south-west (-3,-3 and -4,-2). Crafting table is ~4 blocks to the east-south (+3,+3). Leatherworker villager is ~6 blocks east (+6,+2) with cauldron job site at (+5,+2). All on flat grass with no obstructions. Player has 4 wheat (1 needed to feed), 16 leather (8 for chestplate + 6 for selling + 2 buffer), and 5 emeralds. The villager is level 2 leatherworker with cauldron job site ensuring trade availability. NoAI:1b keeps cows and villager stationary.
